architecture_overview:
haute is a single-process, single-user local insurance-pricing engine: a FastAPI backend + React/TypeScript visual editor whose central artifact is the PipelineGraph (Pydantic model in src/haute/_types.py — nodes, port-aware edges, preamble, submodels). Everything orbits ONE bidirectional contract: the graph is BOTH (a) executed directly over Polars for interactive preview/trace/batch/train/optimise/deploy and (b) round-tripped to standalone Python pipeline files (codegen) that must price identically when run outside the canvas. Semantic equivalence between these two execution modes is the system's defining correctness obligation.

The data model is the hub. From it radiate seven engines: (1) PARSER (src/haute/parser.py + _parser_*.py + _graph_builders.py) turns user-authored decorator-DSL Python into a PipelineGraph (ast path + regex fallback for broken files); (2) CODEGEN (src/haute/codegen.py + _codegen_builders.py) is its inverse, emitting decorated functions + JSON sidecars + connect() calls that ast.parse-validate before write. Parser and codegen form a save/parse fixpoint enforced by Hypothesis round-trip property tests. (3) EXECUTOR (src/haute/executor.py + _execute_lazy.py + chunking.py) runs the graph three ways: eager preview (process-global byte-bounded _preview_cache), fully-lazy batch with adaptive parquet checkpoints, and a fail-loud AST-whitelisted chunked map-reduce. (4) PROJECTION (src/haute/projection.py) is a reverse-topo column-demand planner bounding what execution reads. (5) TRACE (src/haute/trace.py + _trace_*.py + _expression_parser.py) is a pure post-hoc observation layer that correlates a clicked price row backward by value-matching and builds a reconciled waterfall. (6) MODELLING (src/haute/modelling/* + _model_scorer.py + _mlflow_io.py) trains CatBoost/GLM, scores via a uniform ScoringModel, and pins a feature contract. (7) OPTIMISER (src/haute/routes/_optimiser_service.py + bundled Rust price_contour) runs Lagrangian / coordinate-descent price optimisation and efficient frontiers.

The integrity spine is _registry.py (NODE_REGISTRY — exactly one exec AND one codegen builder per NodeType, validated complete at import; KeyError, never silent _gen_transform fallback) plus _cache.py (canonical_json — THE single digest encoder; graph_fingerprint prefixed 'v5:' so an algorithm bump invalidates every keyed entry). Semantic equivalence is structurally defended by SHARING the runtime application helpers between generated bodies and the executor: confirmed in this audit that both src/haute/_builders.py and src/haute/_codegen_builders.py call the identical apply_banding_from_config / apply_rating_step_from_config / score_from_config / execute_edge_join / load_v2_api_source functions — the pricing math has one implementation, not two. The cross-cutting risk surface is therefore NOT the shared math but (a) the WIRING and CONFIG-RESOLUTION layers where generated code and executor independently decide which frame/branch to feed a node (optimiserApply, liveSwitch, constant/source coercion), (b) cache identity/freshness (stat-gated mtime+size fingerprints, the dataframe-cache parquet-artifact lifecycle, two preview/trace caches keyed differently), and (c) broad try/except swallowing in trace enrichment and the expression evaluator that converts bugs into silently-degraded explanations. The whole stack assumes single-process trust (sandbox + path-containment + local-session-token), and the operations layer (deploy/git/databricks/CLI) bridges to the outside world with a test-before-live gate.

ROUTES (src/haute/routes/* + server.py) wire all engines behind a FastAPI app with an in-memory JobStore for long-running train/solve/explore jobs and a WebSocket /ws/sync that pushes graph reloads to the editor. The FRONTEND (frontend/src) mirrors the backend wire contract (api/types.ts validated by types/guards.ts), holds the graph in a Zustand store with tiered undo/redo + a derived dirty flag, and caches per-node results (previews/solves/trains) keyed by a structuralVersion optimistic-concurrency token — its own cache-identity surface that must agree with the backend's notion of 'what changed'.

core_pipelines.name: Author -> Parse -> Edit -> Codegen -> Save (the round-trip fixpoint)
ordered_steps: User authors @pipeline.<type> decorator DSL Python (or `haute init` scaffolds it via _scaffold.py)

parser.parse_pipeline_file -> parse_pipeline_source: ast.parse; on SyntaxError delegate to _parser_regex.fallback_parse (regex-anchored, re-parses recovered fragments with real AST, fail-loud on visible-but-unrecoverable)

_graph_builders._extract_decorated_nodes walks top-level FunctionDefs, _config_builder._resolve_node_config loads JSON sidecar or builds config from literal kwargs, _code_extraction strips codegen boilerplate to recover user code
edges derived: explicit pipeline.connect chains, then implicit param-name matching, then linear-order fallback; submodels resolved recursively + merged via _parser_submodels.merge_submodels
GUI edits node config -> frontend useGraphStore; on save POST /pipeline/save -> routes/_save_pipeline.SavePipelineService

codegen.graph_to_code_multi: validate shape, _error_on_name_collisions (HARD ParseError on sanitize collision), topo-sort, dispatch each node via NODE_REGISTRY[type].codegen, _inject_contract_kwarg via tokenize, _assert_emitted_files_parse ast.parse every file before transactional write
core_pipelines.narrative: Parser and codegen are mutual inverses sharing _code_extraction, _config_io, _graph_shape. The fixpoint invariant (parse(codegen(graph)) structurally equal; codegen(parse(file)) semantically equal) is guarded by Hypothesis round-trip tests. User code is always emitted in STATEMENT form so re-emission is a fixpoint. Generated bodies call the SAME runtime helpers the executor uses, so a standalone pipeline.run() of the saved file is intended to price identically to the canvas.
core_pipelines.failure_surface: SILENT-WRONG sources: (1) Duplicate top-level function names collapse to one GraphNode.id (no de-dup/loud error) — _ast_helpers.py _extract_function_bodies + _graph_builders.py _build_rf_nodes; wrong body attached or node dropped on save. (2) async def @pipeline nodes invisible to the AST parser (only FunctionDef matched) — silent node loss. (3) optimiserApply codegen (_optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source, codegen.py:304-345) returns None and emits a plain `return <first>` when sourceType in {run,registered} and optimiser_mode != 'ratebook', WITHOUT rewiring to the configured ratebook_input, while the executor (_select_optimiser_apply_input, _builders.py:1375-1415) re-derives mode from artifact.get('mode') at runtime and may pick a DIFFERENT frame — saved file and canvas diverge. (4) live_switch generated code hard-routes to the 'live' scenario branch while executor routes by active ctx.source — non-live standalone runs diverge (_codegen_builders.py:521-539 vs _builders.py:633-666). (5) constant/dataSource value coercion (float(val)) emitted-literal vs persisted-config-string round-trip drift. (6) regex-fallback hand-rolled lexer mis-classifying a connect()/decorator as in-string drops an edge silently on already-broken files. (7) submodel name collision overwrites silently (parser.py:198-202); implicit param-name edges into submodel children may be absent from merged graph (_parser_submodels.py:135-168).

core_pipelines.name: Click-node -> Preview (eager) + Click-cell -> Trace (waterfall)
ordered_steps: Frontend selects node -> usePipelineAPI.fetchPreview builds GraphPayload from refs -> POST /pipeline/preview

executor.execute_graph: graph_fingerprint folds row_limit+source+enforce_contracts+projection-suffix+runtime_input_extra_keys; look up process-global _preview_cache (FingerprintCache, 64MB byte-bounded)

miss/partial -> _eager_execute -> _compile_preamble (lru_cache under _preamble_lock) -> _execute_eager_core: prune live-switch edges, topo-walk, enforce column contracts via collect_schema(), project, streaming_collect each node; partial-extend MERGES fresh over cached (fresh wins)
results -> NodeResult dicts -> DataPreview grid; columns written into node.data._columns; downstream cascade (bounded concurrency 4)
Click a cell -> useTracing -> POST /pipeline/trace -> trace.execute_trace reuses _preview_cache (PreviewReader) if full ancestor chain present, else cold _execute_eager_core

_trace_correlation._correlate_rows_posthoc walks backward value-matching each parent row; enrich_steps adds parsed/evaluated expressions + node detail; _trace_waterfall reconciles multiplicative/additive contributions against observed output within float tolerance
core_pipelines.narrative: Preview is cache-first for fast node-switching. Trace is a PURE observation layer reusing the exact DataFrames the user saw, correlating rows post-hoc by value so displayed lineage == preview data. The waterfall is value-derived (delta=after-before) and must reconcile or raises WaterfallReconciliationError (never a silently wrong chart).
core_pipelines.failure_surface: SILENT-WRONG sources: (1) Preview cache is a NON-ATOMIC try_get->execute->store/pin under a process-global cache shared with trace; concurrent same-fingerprint requests race store/pin (pin/unpin imbalance leaks heavy frames). (2) _preamble_lock held only on lru_cache MISS while sys.path/sys.modules mutated globally — a cache HIT thread runs concurrently. (3) _correlate_rows_posthoc positional fast-path with NO shared columns trusts row position for any equal-row-count parent (a sort/cardinality-preserving join could mis-attach the wrong upstream row) — _trace_correlation.py:632-647. (4) _fix_upstream_values relocates rows by fixed 1e-6 ABSOLUTE float tolerance — scale-dependent mis-match at premium/tiny magnitudes (_trace_enrichment.py:1003-1011). (5) enrich_steps wraps every stage in try/except writing an {error} marker — a systematic enricher bug silently degrades every trace while still showing correlation values. (6) _expression_parser evaluator reimplements Polars semantics (null propagation, clip, horizontal funcs) and swallows ALL exceptions to 'opaque' — displayed calculation can silently diverge. (7) execute_trace default row_limit=1000 vs schema 100 — non-route callers correlate against a different row sample.

core_pipelines.name: Upload dataset -> JSON shred -> Cache as parquet -> Execute
ordered_steps: GUI 'Cache as Parquet' -> POST /api/json-cache/build -> routes/json_cache resolves+sandbox-checks data path (resolve_runtime_file_path, enforce_project_root=True)
_json_shred.build_per_port_cache: acquire per-dir build lock, is_per_port_cache_valid no-op trapdoor, record data_file signature (size+mtime_ns, sha256 on mtime drift) BEFORE read
shred_to_buffers single-pass _walk emits one row-set per emitting table (emit AND >=1 selected column), ShredSkipStats counts skipped records/rows

_buffer_to_frame strict-typed Polars (bool-into-numeric/int-into-date rejected) -> one zstd parquet per table with self-describing footer schema + meta.json -> _swap_dir_into_place atomic temp-then-rename (Windows rename retry)
Save -> mirror_cache_to_committed promotes working/ -> committed/ (gated on _session_consulted_hashes)
Execute: _builders/_codegen call load_v2_api_source -> is_per_port_cache_valid(working) else committed -> scan parquets -> LazyFrame routed by sourceHandle port
core_pipelines.narrative: The v2 apiInput codec is content-addressed with a dual working/committed layout and atomic build/swap. Validity requires schema_fingerprint match AND data_file signature match AND a parquet for every emitting table. table_is_emitting is the SINGLE shared predicate across build/validity/load. The build path is serialized per canonical cache dir and atomic so an interrupted build never corrupts a valid cache.
core_pipelines.failure_surface: SILENT-WRONG sources: (1) _v2_fingerprint silently `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns — two structurally different configs collide to the same schema_fingerprint, so a stale cache can be judged fresh (is_per_port_cache_valid/mirror don't re-validate) — _json_shred.py:108-147. (2) cache_state_signature_for_graph keys preview/trace invalidation on int(mtime*1000) — coarse-mtime filesystems can rebuild within one bucket and not invalidate dependents. (3) mirror_cache_to_committed copytree-walks working/->committed/ WITHOUT the build lock — concurrent build dir-swap mid-mirror can copy a torn mix. (4) _resolve_leaf collapses a mid-walk list to cur[0] silently (no skip accounting) — plausible-but-wrong cached column. (5) orjson _read_v2_config keeps last duplicate key while json object_pairs_hook raises — same config accepted differently by cache-build vs parser. (6) stat-gate (mtime_ns,size)-preserved byte change served stale across the whole region (documented accepted blind spot).

core_pipelines.name: Train -> Score -> Explain (model lifecycle)
ordered_steps: POST /api/modelling/train -> _train_service.TrainService.start: validate, merge categorical_levels, estimate safe RAM rows + GPU VRAM (parquet-footer only), execute upstream lazy graph + bounded_sink to temp parquet (column-projected)

TrainingJob.run: _prepare_data (validate schema, remove null-target rows, derive features, snapshot dtypes+categorical_levels) -> _split_data (split_mask 0/1/2 as _partition col) -> _train_model (CatBoost Pool float32 / GLM frame)

_compute_metrics reads diagnostics partition once (holdout>validation>train); SHAP/PDP/Lorenz/AvE optional (failures -> diagnostics_errors, surfaced) -> _save_artifacts native .cbm/.rsglm + per-model {name}.feature_contract.json -> _log_to_mlflow (ModelSignature)

Score: MODEL_SCORE node -> score_from_config -> load_mlflow_model (in-memory LRU 16 + on-disk cache, single-flight per-artifact lock) -> _run_score_pipeline: _validate_features (positional order enforced) -> score_frame explicit per-flavor dispatch -> eager or batched predict
Explain: build one-row Pool/frame -> SHAP/contributions with raw-vs-response additivity self-check -> ranked contribution dict for trace UI
core_pipelines.narrative: Parquet-staged at every stage for bounded memory. config->TrainingJob kwargs single-sourced (build_train_params) so live training and exported scripts can't diverge. Feature contract (sha256 of canonical JSON) pins schema + categorical domains; train/score drift fails loud (assert_contracts_match -> FeatureMismatchError). Eager and batched scoring route proba through one _positive_class_proba_vector.
core_pipelines.failure_surface: SILENT-WRONG sources: (1) pyfunc/RustyStats logged with loader_module='haute._mlflow_io' which has NO module-level _load_pyfunc symbol — mlflow.pyfunc.load_model would fail; masked only because the native .rsglm is loaded separately (_mlflow_log.py:398-476). (2) CatBoost classification: training-metric predict returns proba[:,1] but scoring 'prediction' returns hard label — residual diagnostics mix proba-vs-label semantics. (3) group/temporal split is Bernoulli-per-group with md5 hashing — realised validation fraction can drift far from requested; temporal tie-breaking order-dependent. (4) _validate_features cache keyed on id(model) — id-reuse after GC mitigated only by contract component (fragile to future payload growth). (5) legacy shared feature_contract.json only warned, not removed — stale deploy config validates against wrong model. (6) GLM _align_coefs_and_names prepends (Intercept) heuristically; equal-length mis-ordered coefs/names silently mislabel relativities. (7) stale .haute_cache/output_schema.json keyed only by fingerprint can bake a wrong ModelSignature into deploy.

core_pipelines.name: Solve price optimisation -> Frontier -> Apply/Save/Deploy
ordered_steps: POST /api/optimiser/solve -> OptimiserSolveService.start: flatten graph, find OPTIMISER node, register single-flight job BEFORE heavy work

Setup thread: execute_lazy_graph to data_input, _validate_and_project single streaming pass (reject null quote_id + non-finite obj/constraint/scenario at Float32), sink scored_lf to temp parquet, build_grid_from_parquet_chunked -> Rust QuoteGrid
Solver thread: ONLINE OnlineOptimiser.solve (per-record Lagrangian dual) or RATEBOOK RatebookOptimiser.solve (coordinate descent, fingerprint-aligned factor contexts)

_finalize_solve_result: totals/baseline/lambdas, scenario-value stats, optional inline frontier, persist apply-result + ratebook-factor parquet artifacts behind validated handles, atomic completion with heavy objects retained for a bounded window
Frontier recompute: re-touch solver+grid, enforce compute budget==library cap (10000), cap returned points (2000); frontier-select re-solves ratebook points on demand
Apply/Save/MLflow: build optimiser_result.json (lambdas/factor tables) -> sandbox-validated path; OPTIMISER_APPLY node consumes it via _optimiser_io at runtime/deploy
core_pipelines.narrative: Numerical kernels are bundled Rust (price_contour); haute owns ALL orchestration, streaming, validation, artifact lifecycle, concurrency. Heavy runtime objects (solver/grid/factors) have a short retention TTL after completion; apply/frontier/save re-acquire via touch_heavy_objects and fail loud (400) if evicted — never fabricated. Ratebook factor-level keys are canonicalised to match the apply-side normalise_rating_key (25.0->'25') with loud failure on collapse-collision.
core_pipelines.failure_surface: SILENT-WRONG sources: (1) Inline frontier compute catches ALL exceptions to a non-fatal result['frontier_error'] string while the solve reports success — genuine infeasibility/divergence buried (_optimiser_service.py:2184-2243). (2) Auto-range DROPS entire read-batches containing any null quote_id (counts only the null rows, not co-batched valid quotes) — fail-vs-include asymmetry fragile under future change (1456-1491). (3) legacy frontier_min/max now absolute, applied identically to EVERY constraint regardless of scale — wrong for multi-constraint configs (1366-1406). (4) AUTO_RANGE cache warming advertises solver columns while executing narrower projection — a subset-invariant violation reuses an artifact missing solver columns. (5) ratebook canonical-level minimal-collapse tie -> ValueError mid-save (unsaveable) OR, if level_counts came from a different frame than solved, mis-maps a level to wrong canonical key -> wrong applied rate. (6) frontier-point lambdas reconstructed by string-prefix parsing of lambda_*/total_* keys — naming collision mis-attributes values; ratebook points re-solved may converge to a slightly different optimum than the frontier row implies. (7) the ~5046-LOC god-file duplicates ~10-arm failure-mapping across 4 orchestrators — a fix in one arm easily missed in parallel copies.

subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Translate user-authored decorator-DSL Python into the canonical PipelineGraph; inverse of codegen for the save/parse fixpoint. Two paths: healthy ast-based + regex fallback for broken files.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: Duplicate function-name node collapse (same GraphNode.id) and async-def node invisibility — both silent node loss/corruption on save. Submodel recursion cycle detection (none present). Submodel name-collision silent overwrite and implicit-edge-into-submodel-child drop. Regex-fallback hand-rolled lexer correctness on nested f-strings/implicit concat/byte strings (mis-classified connect drops an edge). Config-folder node aborting the whole fallback parse. Verify the round-trip property test's SKIPPED node types (modelScore/external/liveSwitch/optimiser/submodel) are not under-protected.

subsystem_inventory.subsystem: Codegen (graph -> generated Python) + core graph model
subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: The SAVE side of the fixpoint: emit valid, round-trippable, semantically-faithful pipeline .py. Houses NODE_REGISTRY (single exec+codegen dispatch) and the pricing-semantics helpers shared with the executor.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: THE semantic-equivalence question: confirmed shared helpers (banding/rating/score/edge-join/api-source) but scrutinise WIRING/CONFIG-RESOLUTION divergences — optimiserApply ratebook-input rewiring (codegen returns None vs executor re-derives mode from artifact, HIGH), liveSwitch live-branch hard-route vs ctx.source routing, constant/dataSource float coercion round-trip. Edge-join base/join role assignment at submodel boundaries (build_edge_join_boundary_target_roles 3-tuple lookup — base/join swap silently flips left/right join). _inject_contract_kwarg lexical '(' index before tokenize. rating-key canonicalisation drift between Python mirror (normalise_rating_key) and Polars expr twin (_rating_key_expr). _sanitize_func_name byte-parity with frontend sanitizeName.ts.

subsystem_inventory.subsystem: Execution engine (eager preview / lazy batch / chunked)
subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Run the graph over Polars three ways with memory-bounded admission, adaptive checkpointing, cooperative cancellation, and the process-global preview cache.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: Non-atomic preview-cache read-modify-write under a process-global cache shared with trace (pin/unpin balance, partial-extend merge races). _preamble_lock held only on lru_cache MISS while sys.path/sys.modules mutated globally. Chunked-equivalence whitelist (is_chunk_local_polars_code) — the AST row-local proofs are THE correctness backbone; probe constructs not covered by a property proof. Byte-budget chunk sizing from 128-row sample vs the admission memory budget (wide/variable-width columns underestimate). Contract enforcement at every node boundary (collect_schema) including swallow_errors/preview mode. ExecutionContext memory limit is checkpoint-granular not continuous — a single heavy collect can OOM between checkpoints.

subsystem_inventory.subsystem: Caching & data ingest (fingerprint, LRU, JSON shred, dataframe cache, config IO)
subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Cache identity, integrity and invalidation for preview/trace/dataframe caches + the v2 JSON apiInput parquet codec. Defends 'a key uniquely and deterministically identifies its content'.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: DataFrameExecutionCache parquet-artifact lifecycle (HIGH): scan refcounts + store-window pins + base pins across overridden _is_pinned/_remove_key/_release_scan; the single-unlink rule (entry_before/after path identity) under replacement races — premature unlink (FileNotFoundError on collect) vs leaked parquet. _v2_fingerprint malformed-table silent-continue collision. mtime-bucket invalidation coarseness. mirror_cache_to_committed torn copytree (no build lock). orjson-vs-json duplicate-key divergence. canonical_json as the sole encoder (verify no second encoder leaked back). stat-gate byte-preserving blind spot.

subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Column-demand planning that bounds execution + the post-hoc price-explanation lineage/waterfall. Two coupled correctness surfaces: projection must never silently drop a needed column; trace must never silently show a wrong number.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: Projection: single-parent Polars ordered/unordered demand inference (over/under-demand), fan-in passthrough-parent inference (PolarsFanInRule), rename simultaneity (_demand_before_rename), full-width bailouts for unprovable shapes, projection_rule_coverage completeness. Trace: positional row-correlation fast-path with no shared columns (wrong-row attach), _fix_upstream_values 1e-6 absolute tolerance, enrich_steps catch-all {error} masking, _expression_parser Polars-semantics fidelity + swallow-all-to-opaque, waterfall float reconciliation + JS-safe-integer boundary. Whether enricher bugs surface loudly or hide as per-step errors the UI renders as 'no expression'.

subsystem_inventory.subsystem: Modelling: training, scoring, explainability, MLflow IO
subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Model lifecycle: memory-bounded cancellable training (CatBoost/GLM), uniform ScoringModel with per-flavor casting, SHAP/contribution explainability, MLflow persistence, and the train->score feature contract.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: pyfunc loader_module gap (_load_pyfunc symbol missing) — logged flavor not loadable by standard MLflow. CatBoost classification train-metric (proba) vs scored-prediction (label) semantic mismatch. Feature-order positional enforcement for CatBoost. Model load cache-key fast-path (version='') vs resolved-path agreement + single-flight + disk-cache in-use guard correctness. _validate_features id(model) cache key fragility. group/temporal split fraction balance + tie determinism. GLM coef/name alignment mislabel. Per-flavor predict-frame contract (rustystats raw / pyfunc pandas / catboost float32+_MISSING_). Row alignment (collect-once) so order-unstable upstream can't mis-land predictions.

subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Constrained portfolio price optimisation (Lagrangian + coordinate descent) + efficient frontier, orchestrating the bundled Rust price_contour kernels with full streaming/validation/artifact/concurrency ownership.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: The ~5046-LOC god-file: duplicated ~10-arm failure-mapping across 4 orchestrators (extraction candidate). Inline-frontier swallow-all-to-frontier_error while solve reports success. Auto-range null-quote co-batch exclusion asymmetry + streaming-vs-standard auto-range equivalence. Ratebook factor-level canonicalisation (minimal-collapse tie, level_counts-frame provenance, mixed-dtype). Frontier-point lambda/constraint string-prefix reconstruction + ratebook re-solve convergence. AUTO_RANGE->solver column-superset cache-reuse subset invariant. Heavy-object multi-step touch->get race in apply/frontier paths. legacy frontier_min/max absolute-per-constraint semantics.

subsystem_inventory.subsystem: Routes / API / server / job store / event bus
subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: FastAPI wiring: middleware (request-id, local-session auth, trusted-host), WebSocket file-sync + broadcast, in-process event bus, schemas wire contract, and the in-memory JobStore driving background train/solve/explore jobs.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: JobStore concurrency: atomic whole-dict-swap under _write_lock vs the .jobs property returning _jobs by reference and lock-free background reads (store.jobs.get in ~15 optimiser sites) — torn views on free-threaded 3.13. JobLifecycle reaching into store internals (SLF001) bypassing encapsulation. expected_status guard + reason-precedence correctness. SupersessionCoordinator deferred limiter release via done-callbacks (stranded semaphore permit -> deadlocked key). Heavy-object TTL timer lifecycle (clear-too-early 400s vs never-clear memory growth). WS graph_update dirty-block + source-file path matching + parse_error/graph_update ordering. EventBus typed-payload under-declaration.

subsystem_inventory.subsystem: Platform: sandbox/path security, registry, deploy, CLI, git, databricks
subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: The operations layer between the graph core and the outside world: AST sandbox + restricted unpickler + project-root path containment, the RAM guardrail, git/Databricks wrappers, and deploy packaging with a test-before-live gate.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: Sandbox containment completeness (AST blocklists are the whole story) + the EXECUTOR path resolving config file paths WITHOUT enforce_project_root (asymmetry vs routes — arbitrary-file read if graph JSON is ever attacker-influenced, HIGH). _get_project_root() cwd-at-first-call global (stale/over-broad root weakens every containment check). RestrictedUnpickler broad allowlist still executes reduce machinery. Databricks Windows atomic-replace-vs-open race + first-batch row-loss accounting gap. Token-in-WS-query-string leak.

subsystem_inventory.bounded_context: Browser-side visual editor: Zustand graph store (tiered undo/redo, derived dirty, structural/panel versioning), per-node result caches surviving unmount, typed REST/WS client, trace visualisation, node editors mirroring backend schemas.
subsystem_inventory.phase1_focus: Preview LRU keyed by nodeId alone while freshness depends on (source,rowLimit) — cross-source paint of stale data before refetch (THE wave-2-cache-integrity concern). hashConfig djb2 32-bit collision -> stale solve/train shown as current; sortKeys numeric non-canonicalisation. WS isCurrentSourceFile suffix-matching applying external update to wrong open file. Frontier-point derivation heuristic field resolution (lambda_*/total_*) silent mis-attribution. graphRefreshingRef counter stuck >0 silently disabling undo/redo. guards.ts breadth-vs-test-coverage as the largest schema-drift surface. normalizeEdges admitting edges with non-existent endpoints. App.onUpdateNode synchronous graphRef mutation + store dual-write momentary inconsistency.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Every saved/deployed pipeline. A wrong generated body or wiring prices ALL quotes incorrectly when the pipeline runs standalone or in production, with no canvas signal.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Very high — divergences (optimiserApply frame, liveSwitch branch, edge-join base/join swap, rating-key drift) produce valid-but-wrong Python that ast.parse passes and round-trip structural tests don't catch (they skip these node types). No differential execution test in every case; equivalence rests on shared-helper reuse which does NOT cover config-resolution/wiring.
risk_heatmap.complexity: Very high — graph_to_code_multi (886-1263), tokenize contract injection, per-type builders, submodel boundary handle resolution.
risk_heatmap.rationale: This is THE audit thesis (parse->codegen->execute semantic equivalence). Shared math helpers are confirmed identical, narrowing the threat to the wiring/config layer where two independent decisions (codegen-time vs runtime) can disagree — exactly where the mappers found HIGH-severity optimiserApply and edge-join-role leads. Deep differential-execution dossier required: generate the file, run it, diff against canvas for every node type including the skipped ones.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Stale results served as fresh across preview/trace/dataframe-execution/deploy; or run-failing artifact unlink. Touches every interactive and batch path plus deploy.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Very high — a stale cache hit shows wrong prices with zero error. Multiple documented blind spots: _v2_fingerprint malformed-table collision, mtime-bucket coarseness, stat-gate byte-preserving rewrite, torn mirror copytree. The branch under audit (wave-2-cache-integrity) signals this is the live concern.
risk_heatmap.complexity: Very high — DataFrameExecutionCache 3-overlapping-pin-mechanism artifact lifecycle (304-579, single-unlink rule under replacement races), canonical_json as sole encoder, JSON shred tokenizer.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Cache identity is a named cross-cutting pillar and the active branch. The dataframe-cache parquet lifecycle is the single densest correctness concentration in the codebase (refcounts + weakref finalizers across threads + Windows file-sharing). Fingerprint completeness (does every mutating input appear in a key?) and the dual preview/trace + dataframe cache un-coordinated invalidation are the highest-value scrutiny targets.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Every preview/trace/batch/train/optimise/deploy run. Concurrency bugs corrupt shared caches; chunk-equivalence bugs silently mis-price; memory bugs OOM the process.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: High — non-atomic preview-cache RMW + _preamble_lock-on-miss-only races can serve merged/wrong frames or bind the wrong utility module; chunked!=full would silently diverge if the AST whitelist admits a non-row-local construct.
risk_heatmap.complexity: Very high — execute_graph (~450 lines), _execute_lazy (642-1426), chunk whitelist proofs, admission ledger.
risk_heatmap.rationale: The execution engine is the runtime correctness core and the heaviest concurrency surface (process-global _preview_cache shared with trace, global pl.Config mutation, in-flight reservation ledger). The chunk-locality whitelist is correctness-critical and intricate; each admitted construct must map to a property proof. Concurrent same-fingerprint execute_graph and preamble-lock races are the top concurrency dossiers.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: All optimiser-driven pricing decisions and deployed optimiserApply nodes. Wrong lambdas/factor tables mis-price the whole book.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: High — inline-frontier swallow-all-to-string while solve reports success; auto-range null-co-batch exclusion; ratebook canonical-level mis-map -> wrong applied rate; frontier-point heuristic field reconstruction.
risk_heatmap.complexity: Very high — single ~5046-LOC module with 4 duplicated failure-mapping orchestrators + numerically-subtle Python replay wrappers over Rust.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Highest single-file complexity + multiple silent-numerical leads + a clear architecture (god-file) problem. The Rust kernels are not unit-tested from this repo (only integration), so the Python orchestration/canonicalisation/reconciliation layer is where audit attention pays off. Strong extraction candidate (artifact lifecycle / auto-range engine / factor-table serialisation / failure-mapping).

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Every GUI load and save. Silent node loss/duplication corrupts the saved pipeline file — the user's source of truth.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: High — duplicate function-name node collapse, async-def node invisibility, submodel name-collision overwrite, implicit-edge-into-submodel drop, regex-fallback lexer mis-classification all lose graph structure WITHOUT a loud error, violating the project's fail-loud principle.
risk_heatmap.complexity: High — dual parse paths, recursive submodel merge, hand-rolled fallback lexer, per-kind code extraction.
risk_heatmap.rationale: As the inverse of codegen it shares the fixpoint obligation; a parse-side silent drop combined with a save re-emits a corrupted pipeline. Several concrete fail-loud violations identified (medium-severity each but collectively a systematic gap). Round-trip property tests skip the risky node types and don't cover duplicate names / async / submodel cycles.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Every model-scored price + deployed model artifact. A train/score drift or wrong contract mis-scores production.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Medium-high — pyfunc loader gap (latent, masked by native path), classification proba-vs-label metric mismatch, split fraction drift, stale output_schema baked into deploy signature, legacy shared contract. Mostly bounded by strong fail-loud contract checks.
risk_heatmap.complexity: Very high — parquet-staged training pipeline, dual cache layers, GPU cancellation, per-flavor scoring dispatch.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Feature-contract pinning + assert_contracts_match provide strong drift guards, lowering silent-failure risk relative to codegen/cache. But the model load cache concurrency, the validate-vs-serve artifact divergence (shared with deploy), and classification-metric semantics need a focused dossier. Regression-disciplined per CLAUDE.md.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Projection bug can prune a needed column from BATCH/DEPLOY execution (real missing-column or wrong narrow read). Trace bug shows wrong explanation to actuaries debugging prices (display-only, doesn't change executor output).
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Medium-high — projection bails to full-width on unprovable shapes (conservative, fail-loud-on-real-miss), so its silent surface is the passthrough-parent inference. Trace's enrich_steps catch-all + expression-evaluator swallow-all + 1e-6 row relocation + positional fast-path are genuine silent-wrong-display surfaces.
risk_heatmap.complexity: Very high — projection demand AST analysis (733-1268), trace correlation/enrichment/waterfall, 2232-line expression parser.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Split severity: projection is mostly self-protecting via full-width bailout; trace is explicitly a non-pricing observation layer so wrong values mislead rather than mis-price. The waterfall's hard reconciliation is a strong guard. Audit value concentrates on projection's fan-in passthrough inference and trace's correlation fast-path + catch-all philosophy (tension with fail-loud).

risk_heatmap.subsystem: Routes / server / job store / event bus
risk_heatmap.blast_radius: All HTTP/WS traffic and background job state. A torn job-store read or stranded supersession permit affects job status/availability, not pricing math directly.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Medium — mostly availability/UX (spurious 409/504, stuck job, dropped broadcast) rather than wrong prices; the lock-free .jobs reads are a latent free-threaded-Python hazard, benign on current CPython.
risk_heatmap.complexity: High — JobStore TTL+heavy-object timers, SupersessionCoordinator condition state machine, WS broadcast.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Concurrency-dense but the failure modes are predominantly reliability/observability, not silent mispricing. Highest-value items: the JobStore encapsulation break (lifecycle poking privates), supersession deferred-release deadlock, and heavy-object timer lifecycle. Lower correctness-blast than the pricing engines.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Sandbox/path: whole-host file access if breached. Deploy: validate-vs-serve gap ships behaviour the gate didn't test. Mostly operational boundaries.
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Medium — deploy validate-vs-serve artifact divergence and liveSwitch pruner label-collision are silent dev-vs-prod mispricing; sandbox gaps are loud-or-exploit not silent-wrong. RAM-estimate 4GiB fallback can silently OOM or over-downsample.
risk_heatmap.complexity: High — RAM column-set BFS, deploy resolve/prune/bundle, git state machine, databricks streaming integrity.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Security boundary is heavily tested; the sharper correctness leads are the executor's enforce_project_root asymmetry (HIGH, arbitrary-file read) and the deploy validate-vs-serve divergence (HIGH, the test-before-live gate may not exercise shipped artifacts). These two cross into the pricing-correctness story and warrant a focused dossier; the rest is solid operational code.

risk_heatmap.blast_radius: Browser-only: wrong cached preview/solve shown to one user, or undo/redo silently disabled. Never persists wrong prices to disk (save captures a fresh snapshot).
risk_heatmap.silent_failure_potential: Medium — cross-source preview paint and djb2 config-collision show stale/wrong data as current to the user, but the backend is the source of truth and saves are explicit. The wave-2 branch name suggests the preview-cache-keying issue is the active concern.
risk_heatmap.complexity: High — usePipelineAPI cascade, frontier-point derivation, tiered graph store, WS lifecycle, 1922-line guards.ts.
risk_heatmap.rationale: Lowest correctness-blast (display-layer, ephemeral, backend-authoritative) but directly named by the audit branch (wave-2-cache-integrity) — the nodeId-only preview cache key vs (source,rowLimit) freshness is the headline frontend cache-integrity item. guards.ts breadth-vs-test-coverage is the schema-drift risk. Worth a targeted dossier on the cache-keying and frontier-derivation, not a full deep audit.

cross_cutting_concerns.summary: The system's defining obligation: a graph executed in-canvas must price identically to the same graph round-tripped to a standalone .py and run via pipeline.run(). The architecture defends this by SHARING runtime helpers — confirmed in this audit that src/haute/_builders.py (executor) and src/haute/_codegen_builders.py (generated bodies) both import and call the SAME apply_banding_from_config / apply_rating_step_from_config / score_from_config / execute_edge_join / load_v2_api_source. So the pricing MATH has one implementation. The residual threat is the WIRING + CONFIG-RESOLUTION layer, where codegen (at save time) and the executor (at run time) make INDEPENDENT decisions about which frame/branch feeds a node and can disagree.
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: Highest. CONFIRMED divergence: optimiserApply codegen returns None and emits a plain passthrough return (no rewiring to ratebook_input) when sourceType in {run,registered} and optimiser_mode != 'ratebook', while the executor re-derives mode from the loaded artifact.get('mode') and may select a different input frame. liveSwitch generated code hard-routes to the 'live' branch while the executor routes by ctx.source. Edge-join base/join role at submodel boundaries can silently swap left/right. Build a DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION harness: codegen a graph, run the file, diff outputs against execute_graph for every node type — especially the ones the round-trip property test SKIPS (modelScore/external/liveSwitch/optimiser/optimiserApply/scenarioExpander/submodel).

cross_cutting_concerns.theme: Cache identity & integrity (key uniqueness + artifact lifecycle + freshness)
cross_cutting_concerns.summary: Multiple cache layers each assert 'a key uniquely and deterministically identifies its content': graph_fingerprint ('v5:' prefix, canonical_json sole encoder) for preview/trace; dataframe_execution_cache_key (lineage-scoped) for materialized frames; the v2 JSON-shred schema_fingerprint + data_file signature for ingest; stat-gated (mtime_ns,size) for artifacts. The active branch is wave-2-cache-integrity. Three failure classes: (a) key INCOMPLETENESS — a mutating input not folded into the key serves stale; (b) artifact LIFECYCLE — the dataframe cache unlinks parquet via weakref.finalize + refcounts + pins across threads, where a single-unlink-rule slip either unlinks a live artifact (run-failing) or leaks disk; (c) FRESHNESS resolution — stat-gate mtime+size and mtime-bucket invalidation have documented blind spots.
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: Highest (tied with semantic equivalence; it is the named branch). Two distinct dossiers: (1) the DataFrameExecutionCache parquet-artifact lifecycle under concurrent replacement + Windows file-sharing — the densest correctness code in the repo; (2) fingerprint COMPLETENESS audit — enumerate every input class that affects output (file bytes, schema, model artifact, preamble utility module, categorical levels) and prove each appears in the relevant key, plus reconcile the two preview/trace vs dataframe cache key surfaces and the frontend nodeId-only preview cache vs (source,rowLimit) freshness.

cross_cutting_concerns.theme: Error-handling philosophy: fail-loud mandate vs broad try/except silent degradation
cross_cutting_concerns.summary: CLAUDE.md mandates fail-loud, no band-aid fallbacks. The codebase mostly honours this (ParseError on non-literal kwargs, KeyError on missing registry entry, ContractMismatchError at every node boundary, WaterfallReconciliationError, FeatureMismatchError, FetchIntegrityError). But several hot paths VIOLATE it with broad catch-alls that convert real bugs into silent degradation: trace enrich_steps wraps every stage in try/except -> {error} marker; _expression_parser parse/evaluate swallow ALL exceptions -> 'opaque'/row[target]; inline optimiser frontier catches all -> result['frontier_error'] string while reporting success; codegen MODEL_SCORE contract falls back to 'opaque' on infra error; routes/_helpers load_sidecar swallows corrupt JSON -> {}.
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: High. For each catch-all, classify: is the swallowed failure truly non-fatal (one bad trace step shouldn't poison the trace) or does it hide a wrong NUMBER / wrong cache decision? The trace/expression swallowing is the worst because a systematic enricher bug degrades every explanation invisibly; the frontier swallowing buries genuine infeasibility under a 'success'. Recommend: narrow the catch to expected exceptions, surface a distinct warning state, and assert in tests that a deliberate enricher/evaluator bug surfaces loudly.

cross_cutting_concerns.summary: Single-process multi-threaded FastAPI with many process-global mutable singletons: executor._preview_cache (shared with trace.py, non-atomic try_get->execute->store/pin RMW); _preamble_lock held only on lru_cache MISS while sys.path/sys.modules mutate globally; _polars_utils global pl.Config chunk-size under a lock affecting all concurrent Polars work; _execution_admission in-flight reservation ledger; DataFrameExecutionCache refcounts+pins+weakref-finalizers running on arbitrary GC threads; JobStore whole-dict-swap vs lock-free .jobs reads (~15 optimiser sites) + JobLifecycle poking privates; SupersessionCoordinator deferred-release via done-callbacks; _sandbox._get_project_root cwd-at-first-call global; git/databricks/joblib module-global locks.
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: High. The preview-cache RMW race + the preamble-lock-on-miss race are the two most likely to produce SILENT wrong results (served merged entry / wrong utility module bound). The dataframe-cache finalizer-on-GC-thread + replacement races are correctness-and-resource. The lock-free JobStore reads are latent (benign on CPython, hazardous on free-threaded 3.13 which the code already anticipates). Stress-test concurrent same-fingerprint execute_graph and the supersession deferred-release under cancellation.

cross_cutting_concerns.summary: Pricing is float-precision-sensitive and several places reimplement or canonicalise numerics in two parallel forms that must agree. Rating-key canonicalisation has a Python mirror (normalise_rating_key) AND a Polars expr twin (_rating_key_expr) that must produce identical keys (drift -> silent table miss -> defaultValue/neutral instead of intended rate). The trace expression evaluator reimplements Polars arithmetic/null/conditional semantics in Python. _fix_upstream_values uses a fixed 1e-6 ABSOLUTE float tolerance (scale-dependent). Ratebook factor-level canonicalisation collapses int-like floats to match the apply join. Constant/dataSource nodes coerce via float(val) in two places. The model feature contract pins dtypes; CatBoost casts float32 vs GLM keeps native. canonical_json defines deterministic NaN/Inf tokens for digest material, separate from JSON-wire to_json_safe.
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: Medium-high. The rating-key Python-mirror-vs-Polars-twin agreement is the highest-value numerical dossier (drift silently mis-prices via table miss, and BOTH codegen and executor route through it). The ratebook factor-level canonicalisation -> apply-join key agreement is the optimiser analogue. The trace 1e-6 absolute tolerance and the expression-evaluator Polars fidelity are display-only (waterfall reconciles) but still erode explainability trust. Test these against REAL Polars output, not the reimplementation's own behaviour.

cross_cutting_concerns.theme: Security & trust boundary (sandbox, path containment, local auth)
cross_cutting_concerns.summary: Single-user local trust model with defence-in-depth: AST sandbox (validate_user_code blocklists) + restricted builtins (safe_globals) + RestrictedUnpickler allowlist + project-root path containment (validate_project_path/validate_safe_path/resolve_runtime_file_path) + LocalSessionMiddleware (hmac token + local Origin) + git argument-injection guards + Databricks SQL allowlist. The boundary is mostly solid and heavily tested, but has asymmetries: the EXECUTOR resolves config file paths with enforce_project_root defaulting False (vs routes' True) — arbitrary-file read at execution if a graph's config is ever attacker-influenced; _get_project_root caches cwd at first call (over-broad root weakens everything); the session token is also accepted as a WS URL query param (logs/referrers leak); _is_local_origin treats absent Origin as trusted.
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: Medium-high for the executor enforce_project_root asymmetry (the one lead that crosses from 'operational' into a real exploit surface if graph JSON provenance is ever untrusted, e.g. shared/imported pipelines); medium for the rest. The sandbox blocklist completeness is well-tested (~1700-line test file) but adversarial — worth confirming the blocklist vs known CPython escape vectors stays current. Document whether 'pipeline source is trusted code' is the intended invariant and that no route builds a graph from request data before the path check.

cross_cutting_concerns.summary: Interactive responsiveness vs bounded memory on large data. Hot paths: ast.parse on every GUI load + multiple full-source textual rescans (regex fallback O(n^2)); _expression_parser re-parses the same code up to 5x per column; preview cache + preamble lru_cache make node-switching O(serialise); lazy batch adds adaptive parquet checkpoints to break Polars plan duplication (#24206) + chained-join accumulation; chunked path streams with bounded memory; dataframe-execution cache spills frames to parquet; model loads cached in-memory(16)+on-disk(50); frontend recomputes structural/panel fingerprints via JSON.stringify of all node configs on every history-aware edit (O(config size), a hotspot for large rating tables).
cross_cutting_concerns.phase1_priority: Medium. Performance is well-engineered (checkpointing, caching, projection pushdown are deliberate and sophisticated). Lower audit priority than correctness, but two leads intersect correctness: the byte-budget chunk sizing (128-row sample) can UNDER-bound memory vs the admission budget (a bounded-memory promise broken silently under wide data), and the frontend per-edit fingerprint cost on large ratebooks. Profile rather than deep-audit unless a memory-safety regression appears.

open_questions: SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE — is there ANY differential-execution test (codegen a graph -> run the .py -> diff against execute_graph) for the node types the round-trip property test explicitly skips (modelScore/externalFile/liveSwitch/modelling/optimiser/optimiserApply/scenarioExpander/submodel/submodelPort)? The mappers found the property test uses only 2-5 linear-edge graphs and asserts STRUCTURE not VALUES, so the confirmed optimiserApply/liveSwitch wiring divergences may be entirely unguarded. This is the single most important Phase-1 question.

OPTIMISER_APPLY divergence — confirmed in code: codegen (_optimiser_apply_ratebook_return_source) emits a plain passthrough when sourceType in {run,registered} and optimiser_mode != 'ratebook', while the executor (_select_optimiser_apply_input) re-derives mode from artifact.get('mode'). Is there a real scenario where a saved/deployed pipeline applies the optimiser to a different frame than the canvas, and does any test pin standalone-run == canvas-run for a ratebook optimiserApply with an MLflow-sourced artifact whose mode resolves to 'ratebook' only at runtime?

DATAFRAME CACHE LIFECYCLE — under concurrent same-key replacement plus a late-running weakref.finalize on a GC thread (especially Windows file-sharing), can the single-unlink rule (_remove_key vs _release_scan entry_before/after path identity, lines 527-579) ever (a) unlink a parquet a live LazyFrame still scans -> CacheArtifactMissing on collect, or (b) orphan a parquet forever? Needs a targeted concurrency/GC-timing stress test.

FINGERPRINT COMPLETENESS — is EVERY input class that affects execution output represented in the relevant cache key? Specifically: does the preview/trace key capture model-artifact changes (an out-of-band MLflow re-log), and do the two surfaces (runtime_input_extra_keys stat-gated memo vs dataframe_graph_input_fingerprint content hash) ever DISAGREE for the same logical input, serving stale from one cache while the other invalidates?

RATING-KEY TWIN AGREEMENT — do the Python mirror (normalise_rating_key) and the Polars expr twin (_rating_key_expr) provably produce identical keys across the full dtype matrix (Float32 non-integer, plain-string '25' on a float column, Int64-range boundaries, legacy '25.0' sidecar keys)? A drift silently yields defaultValue/neutral instead of the intended rate, and BOTH codegen-emitted and executor code route through it. Is there a differential test against real Polars?

DEPLOY VALIDATE-vs-SERVE — validate_deploy/score_test_quotes run test quotes through score_graph WITHOUT artifact_paths/remap, while the deployed container/pyfunc DOES pass them. Does the test-before-live gate therefore actually exercise the SAME bundled artifacts (model/optimiser) the deployed scorer uses, or can a deploy pass validation yet score differently in production?

EXECUTOR PATH CONTAINMENT — is the asymmetry intentional that execution.py resolves config file paths with enforce_project_root defaulting False while HTTP routes pass True? Is 'pipeline source/graph JSON is fully trusted' a documented invariant, and is there any route or import path (shared/imported submodels, deploy) that constructs a graph from less-trusted data and then executes it before a path check?

TRACE ERROR PHILOSOPHY — does any test assert that a SYSTEMATIC enricher bug (wrong column) or an expression-evaluator bug surfaces LOUDLY rather than degrading every trace step to a benign {error} the UI renders as 'no expression detected'? The catch-all in enrich_steps (1816-1838) and the swallow-all-to-opaque in parse_expression (988-1003) directly contradict the fail-loud mandate — is this an intentional, tested exception or an unaudited gap?

PREVIEW-CACHE CONCURRENCY — under concurrent execute_graph requests on the SAME fingerprint (interleaved partial-extend + full-miss), is the non-atomic try_get->_eager_execute->store/pin sequence proven to keep pin/unpin balanced (no leaked pinned heavy DataFrame inflating RSS) and to never persist a partially-merged wrong entry? The mappers flagged no test for this exact interleaving.

FRONTEND CACHE KEYING (wave-2 headline) — the preview LRU slot is keyed by nodeId alone while freshness depends on (source, rowLimit), so switching activeSource paints the other source's cached rows before refetch. Is this the specific defect the wave-2-cache-integrity branch targets, and does the existing previewCache.test.ts cover the source/rowLimit collapse (the mapper says it does NOT)?

DUPLICATE/ASYNC NODES — what is the intended behaviour when two @pipeline.<type> functions share a name (collapse to one GraphNode.id) or a node is `async def` (invisible to the AST parser)? Both are currently SILENT losses violating fail-loud; should the parser raise a loud ParseError, and is the absence of any test for these confirmed?

GOD-FILE FAILURE-MAPPING DRIFT — _optimiser_service.py duplicates ~10-arm exception->lifecycle-transition+metrics+cleanup logic across 4 orchestrators (solve setup, two auto-range drivers, solver). Have all four copies stayed in sync, or has a fix to one failure arm been missed in a parallel copy (e.g. orphan-artifact cleanup or terminal-reason mapping)? This is both a correctness and an extraction-candidate question.
